titulo: Difficult pronouns and prepositions: Personal «a» and object pronouns

aula.objetivo: Use the personal «a» confidently, recognise leísmo without adopting it, choose the right preposition after common verbs (including «de que»), review «por» and «para», and place pronouns correctly with infinitives, gerunds and imperatives.

itens.pt: to know someone, to meet someone
to love someone, to be fond of someone

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the direct object is whoever receives the action of the verb: «Veo la casa», «Veo a Ana». When that object is a specific person, Spanish puts «a» before it: «Veo a Ana» (I see Ana), «Llamo a mi hermano» (I'm calling my brother). This is the personal «a», and English has nothing like it — it isn't translated. STEP 2: the personal «a» is also used for a pet with a name or one you love («Quiero mucho a mi gato»), and with «alguien», «nadie» and «quién» («No veo a nadie», «¿A quién esperas?» — Who are you waiting for?). STEP 3: it isn't used after «tener», or after «hay» to say what there is: «Tengo dos hermanos», «Hay muchos estudiantes». STEP 4: it isn't used with things: «Busco un hotel», not «busco a un hotel». STEP 5: with an unspecified person (anyone at all), the «a» disappears: «Busco un médico que hable alemán»; with a specific person, it comes back: «Busco al médico de mi madre». STEP 6: the direct object pronouns are «lo» (him, it), «la» (her, it), «los» and «las»; the indirect object pronouns are «le» (to him, to her, to you-usted) and «les». «Lo vi» = I saw him (Pablo); «Le di el libro» = I gave him/her the book. STEP 7: CAUTION, leísmo: in Spain many people say «le» instead of «lo» when the direct object is a man: «Le vi ayer» instead of «Lo vi ayer». The standard accepts this only for a single male person. In Latin America «lo» dominates. STEP 8: laísmo («La dije la verdad») and loísmo («Lo di un libro») are considered incorrect: what you give or say to someone is an indirect object, so the pronoun is «le», whether it's a man or a woman: «Le dije la verdad», «Le di un libro». STEP 9: as a learner, use «lo» and «la» for direct objects and «le» for indirect objects; recognise leísmo when you hear it, without needing to adopt it.
blocos.comparacao: English "I see Ana" and "I'm calling my brother" have no preposition, but Spanish requires «a» before a specific person: «veo a Ana», «llamo a mi hermano». English "I have two brothers" → «tengo dos hermanos», with no «a». And English "him/her" doesn't tell you direct from indirect, but Spanish does: «lo/la» (direct) vs «le» (indirect): «La veo» (I see her) × «Le digo la verdad» (I tell her the truth).

exemplos.ru: Veo a Ana todos los días.
Busco un médico que hable alemán.
exemplos.pt: I'm looking for a doctor who speaks German (any doctor).

exemplos.ru: Busco al médico de mi madre.
exemplos.pt: I'm looking for my mother's doctor (a specific one).
I love my cat very much.

exemplos.ru: Lo vi ayer en la calle. (Pablo)
exemplos.pt: I saw him in the street yesterday. (Pablo)

exemplos.ru: Le dije la verdad a mi madre.
exemplos.pt: I told my mother the truth.

erros.certo: Veo a Ana todos los días.
erros.motivo: A specific person as direct object takes «a».
What you say to someone is an indirect object: «le», for either gender.

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences with the personal «a»: «Veo a… Llamo a… Espero a… Conozco a… Invito a… Quiero a…». Then repeat three of them replacing the object with a pronoun: «La llamo», «Los invito».
Review lesson 59. Explain out loud, without naming them, two household objects with «sirve para» and «se parece a».
